summary: Hetzner Cloud tool pack, built for output compression rather than API access: hcloud already wraps the API, so these two correlate across sources and print only what changes a decision. baseline-audit.py scores one box against a CIS-derived baseline by joining the account side (firewall attached, SSH open to the world, Cloud Backups paid for and the snapshot age) with box-side evidence the caller already gathered from sshd -T, ss -tulpnH and sysctl -a, never shelling out and never running a command on the host; it prints one line per failing item, treats unverifiable as unmet, prices the Backups surcharge, holds every auto-fix when no out-of-band escape is verified, and refuses the run outright when an expired waiver is still covering a failing item. fw-sync.py converges a cloud firewall from the same spec behind the guard that justifies the tool: set_rules is a destructive replace, so it proves inbound SSH survives for every admin CIDR and for the caller's own source before any write, exits 5 rather than locking anyone out, and arms a revert of the prior rule set that only a second invocation carrying --commit can cancel. Neither can delete a server, volume, snapshot or image; Hetzner Robot dedicated servers are out of scope.

credentials.min_scope: one project-scoped API token; Read is enough for baseline-audit and is what it should be given, Read & Write only for fw-sync. Hetzner tokens are project-wide with no per-resource scoping, so use a separate token per project and never a token that also reaches production data volumes
